newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks seen higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks seen higher at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to follow through on Wednesday's rally at the open on Thursday and move higher.

Analysts warned an upward move would be limited by anticipation of Friday's February jobs data and the fact that Wednesday's rally was the result of relief after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan eased fears the Fed may be planning a rate hike to slow the stock market's runup.
"We're not out of the woods yet," said Peter Cardillo, director of Research at Westfalia Investments.

"Of course, Greenspan made an effort to say his past comments were not intended to bring stock prices down," Cardillo said. "The next question, the really big question, is interest rates and will the Fed make any pre-emptive strikes."
He said that the market would probably have a higher opening as bonds and the S&P 500 Index futures contract were slightly higher, but he added that strength may be short-lived.

"I would not be surprised to see a reversal today as the market positions itself for tomorrow's employment report," Cardillo said. "If there are any substantial increases in wage pressure, the Fed could hike rates."
